rubriker.title: Samarkand R7 (open): Uzbekistan continue dominating run, extend lead
rubriker._rss_content: Uzbekistan opened a two-point lead in the Chess Olympiad after defeating China 3–1 in round seven, with Nodirbek Abdusattorov and Nodirbek Yakubboev scoring the decisive wins. The hosts remain the only team unbeaten on every individual board. Armenia, India, Germany, the Netherlands and Azerbaijan form the chasing group. On Wednesday, Armenia drew the United States, while the remaining four chasers all won their round-seven encounters. | Photo: Rafal Oleksiewicz / FIDE

rubriker.title: Round 7 Recap: Uzbekistan extend their lead as India stay in the hunt
rubriker._rss_content: Round 7 saw Uzbekistan strengthen their lead, while India kept their medal hopes alive and Praggnanandhaa produced the day’s standout win

rubriker.title: The Two Nodirbeks Keep Uzbekistan Perfect Through Seven Rounds
rubriker._rss_content: Round seven pitted the Open section's top two teams directly against each other, and Uzbekistan didn't blink. Beating China 3-1, the hosts pushed their record to a perfect 7-0-0 and opened up a lead big enough that even a loss next round wouldn't cost them top spot outright.

rubriker.title: Behind the scenes in Samarkand: The playing hall
rubriker._rss_content: The ChessBase crew continues its coverage from the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, moving from the exhibition stand to the playing hall and capturing some of the atmosphere around the event. The latest vlog features reactions to the forthcoming ChessBase for Mac, behind-the-scenes work by the team, new guests in the "Off the Board" interview series and the celebrations that follow a victory by the Uzbek team.

rubriker.title: Total Chess World Championship Tour announces six more stars for pilot
rubriker._rss_content: The 24-player field for the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest is now complete, with Levon Aronian, Le Quang Liem, Jorden van Foreest, Abhimanyu Mishra, Shakhriyar Mamedyarov and Andrew Hong joining the lineup. The FIDE-approved event, scheduled for 10–20 November, will combine Fast Classic, Rapid and Blitz in a single competition and serve as the pilot for the global Total Chess World Championship Tour launching in 2027.

rubriker._rss_content: Det norske herrelaget i Sjakk-OL skuffet i syvende runde, hvor det ble et knapt nederlag 1½-2½ mot Chile. Det norske lyspunktet var GM Johan-Sebastian Christiansen (2656) på førstebord, som vant med hvit mot GM Rodrigo Vasquez Schroeder (CHI 2457) uten noensinne å så dårligst underveis. rubriker.title: Australian Chess Player Denied Bail in Stalking Case
rubriker._rss_content: An Australian chess player has been denied bail while facing 35 charges, including allegations of stalking and intimidating a female chess streamer.

rubriker.title: Rosenstein takes FIDE rules dispute to CAS
rubriker._rss_content: Wadim Rosenstein has appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, seeking an independent review of how FIDE’s existing sanctions rules should be applied consistently in its presidential election.

rubriker.title: Ajedrez educativo como respuesta a los desafíos de PISA 2025
rubriker._rss_content: El informe PISA 2025 vuelve a poner en primer plano el deterioro de competencias fundamentales como la lectura, las matemáticas y la atención sostenida. A partir de este diagnóstico, el texto examina por qué el ajedrez puede resultar relevante para la educación: comparte estructuras con el razonamiento matemático y la lectura crítica, aunque su transferencia al rendimiento escolar exige una mediación pedagógica explícita, planificación docente y un uso más cuidadoso de la tecnología. | Imagen (IA): Uvencio Blanco
